extraction_notes:
LANE A (patents) and LANE B (sequence/chemistry panels) were run together because the highest-yield sequence/chemistry panels turned out to be inside US patents.

RETRIEVAL. USPTO print PDFs (image-ppubs.uspto.gov/.../downloadPdf/<number>) are image-only - PyMuPDF extracts 0 characters of text from all 113 pages of US11535849 - so they were useless without OCR. All patent text and, crucially, all patent TABLE STRUCTURE came from Google Patents HTML (patents.google.com/patent/<pub>/en), parsed cell-by-cell with a <tr>/<td> parser rather than from flattened text. patents.google.com returns intermittent HTTP 503; retries with backoff were needed. The Google Patents XHR search endpoint (/xhr/query) works but rejects double quotes and field-restricted syntax (CL=, AB=), which limited phrase searching; assignee= as a separate parameter does work.

HAZARD 1 - naive sequence regex vs declared length. Confirmed as real. In US 2023/0263822 A1 a plain [ACGT]-run scan produced 94 corrupted entries: line-wrapped sequence cells silently yielded truncated sequences (e.g. ISIS 416825 as the 12-mer 'GCCCTTCATGTC' instead of the 20-mer 'GCCCTTCATGTCTAGGTCCA'). Every sequence in this file was therefore accepted only after its length matched an INDEPENDENTLY DECLARED length in the same row: for the TTR patent, both (stop site - start site + 1) AND the sum of the gapmer motif; for the FXI patent, the motif sum; for the Factor VII patent, the length of the per-position sugar-chemistry string. Anything that failed was dropped, not repaired by guessing. Cross-validation: ISIS 416858 was recovered independently from two different patents and agrees (ACGGCATTGGTGCACAGTTT, 5-10-5 MOE); ISIS 420915 matches the published inotersen sequence.

HAZARD 2 - chemistry encoded by rendering, not by letters. Encountered in a different form than warned. In the Ionis patents chemistry is stated in prose ('5-10-5 MOE gapmers... internucleoside linkages are phosphorothioate... all cytidines are 5-methylcytidines') or as an explicit per-position string (Factor VII Table 37: 'eeeeeddddddddddeeeee'), so no case inference was needed. In PMC12846741 the chemistry is encoded by FONT COLOUR in Supplementary Table S1 (orange = LNA, red = 2'-OMe, black = DNA, italic = RNA). That was resolved from the PDF TEXT LAYER by reading each span's colour attribute via PyMuPDF get_text('dict') - giving 3-10-3 LNA gapmers - never by looking at rendered pixels. The same legend encodes PS vs PO by UNDERLINE, which is not recoverable from the text layer, so backbone_chemistry and ps_count for those five constructs are TBD rather than guessed.

WHAT WAS DROPPED AND WHY. (a) US 2023/0263822 A1 Table 75: its 'Platelets (10^3/uL)' column reads 18 for the PBS rat control, and the companion Table 76 shows haemoglobin as '6' - the table is evidently not reporting means, so all 12 rows were dropped rather than published as counts. (b) US 11,535,849 B2 Table 59, ISIS 420959: printed 'n.d.'. (c) US 2023/0263822 A1 Table 66 weeks 4 and 6: the PBS control is 'n.d.' at those timepoints, so there is no concurrent control to grade against; only week 2 was taken. (d) US 9,322,021 B2 platelet-aggregation table: on-target antithrombotic pharmacology (FeCl3 thrombosis model), not oligo-induced platelet toxicity. (e) PMC10294360: platelet data are disease-group, not per-compound.

UNIT AND CAPTION DEFECTS PRESERVED, NOT SILENTLY CORRECTED. US 2015/0031747 A1 Table 45 is captioned 'Complement C3 levels in cynomolgus monkeys' but its columns are platelet and RBC counts. US 2023/0263822 A1 Table 158 prints '(x100/uL)' where the values and the companion Table 137 both indicate x10^3/uL. Several tables print '10^3/mL' where '10^3/uL' is meant. In each case the value was recorded with the physiologically coherent unit and the discrepancy is spelled out in the row's notes.

GRADING. Rodent/NHP platelet-count rows use one stated convention: change vs the concurrent PBS control greater than -10% = grade 0; -10% to -30% = grade 1; worse than -30% = grade 2. The grade-2 cut-off is anchored to the patents' own screening language - US 11,535,849 B2 advances only compounds that 'did not affect a decrease in platelet count less than 70% of the PBS control', and US 2023/0263822 A1 uses a 50% cut-off - so a >30% decline is a finding those sponsors themselves treated as disqualifying. No rodent or NHP count fell near 100x10^9/L, so no grade 3 was assigned from a count. In-vitro rows follow the schema rubric: activation markers only, at supra-clinical concentration = 1; clear aggregation = 2. The single grade 3 in this file is the pulmonary haemorrhage plus lethality reported for Dmpk Chol-ASO, and it is flagged is_platelet_specific = FALSE because the paper does not prove the bleeding was platelet-mediated.

NO NUMBER IN THIS FILE WAS RECALLED OR INFERRED. Every readout_value is either a figure literally present in a fetched table, or TBD. Rows whose values exist only inside a figure image (all PMC12846741 and PMC7063478 rows) carry readout_value = TBD with the direction taken verbatim from the authors' own sentence; those sentences are quoted in the notes.

IDENTITY CAVEAT. The patent prints only 'Compound No. 957943'. It is joined here under the INN 'fesomersen' on the basis of AdisInsight and Synapse drug records (ION-957943 = IONIS-FXI-LRx = BAY 2976217 = fesomersen), not on the basis of the patent text; one aggregator (BioCentury) merges the fesomersen and IONIS-FXIRx profiles, so a curator should sanity-check this join key. The unconjugated parent is kept separate as 'ISIS 416858'.

NOT REACHED. The most valuable remaining targets are US 10,927,377 B2 (APOL1; four platelet tables including cynomolgus Table 103) and US 10,100,310 B2 (PKK; cynomolgus Table 54), both already downloaded and confirmed to contain platelet tables of the same form. Roche/AstraZeneca/Alnylam assignee searches returned no patent whose examples carry per-compound platelet readouts; the Roche in-vitro platelet risk work appears in the literature (Sewing 2017) rather than in a granted patent I could locate. Europe PMC searches for further multi-compound platelet panels surfaced mostly single-compound or review material beyond the two CC-BY papers used here.
